Hi Marta — thanks for the RFP and the clear questions. Short answers up-front, then attaching a two-page comparison (RDW_Optimize_Starter-vs-Scale.pdf). Happy to walk through on a quick call if you prefer.

Bullets:
- Starter: host-mode default is conservative batching (target latency SLOs) with opportunistic KV/prefix caching. Typical batch windows are 5–10ms; good for low-to-medium concurrency. Expect 95th p99s comparable to hosted benchmarks in doc; 99th depends on burst patterns.
- Scale (dedicated): allows more aggressive batching (larger batch windows, adaptive micro-batching) because you control pool capacity. We proactively keep warm KV cache for pinned models so cache hit rates for repeated contexts can exceed 70–80% for stable traffic, reducing per-token compute.
- Quantization: recommended path depends on model family. Q4_0 or Q4_K_M can retain >98% of quality vs fp16 on many Llama-family variants for short-form QA. INT8 (where supported) gives best cost wins but may need evals on your testset — we typically gate int8 for generative QA unless tolerances are known. We can run a 3-model small eval and show numeric deltas (Rouge/F1).
- Pilot credits/discounts: standard pilot bundle is $Xk credit + 10% technical discount for POCs that progress to committed reserved capacity within 90 days. We can tailor pilot credits for procurement constraints.

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick 30-min tech sync (Aditya can run the eval plan); 2) draft a short pilot SOW (attached). Monica will scope commercial options and concession bands.

Thanks — available Tue/Wed late-morning PST.

On Mon, Nov 1, 2027 at 4:10 PM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Starter: host-mode default is conservative batching (target latency SLOs) with opportunistic KV/prefix caching. Typical batch windows are 5–10ms; good for low-to-medium concurrency.

Hi Marta — quick technical breakdown to help with your procurement evaluation and the QA scoring you mentioned.

Summary (short):
- Starter (hosted):
  * Batching: latency-first micro-batching; targets 5–15ms scheduling windows, adaptive by token stage. Good for pilots where you expect <200 concurrent reqs.
  * Cache: prefix caching available but shared; expected cold-starts on scale-up. Hit-rate depends on reuse — for chat sessions with repeated prompts expect 25–40% hit initially.
  * Quant: we default to Q4_0 on lighter models in Starter for cost parity; some models are fp16-only in hosted catalog.
- Scale (dedicated):
  * Batching: continuous batching + backlog shaping — batch windows grow with pool throughput, can hit 30–100ms batching during high throughput to amortize per-token cost while still hitting 100–200ms p99 depending on model/seq.
  * Cache: customer-managed per-tenant cache; warm-start strategies (preload keys) can push hit-rates to 70%+ for conversationally repetitive flows.
  * Quant: full control to deploy INT8/Q4 variants; we recommend staged rollout: Q4 eval -> blind int8 eval -> limited canary.

Practical guidance for your eval set (we can run these):
1) Run the baseline fp16 on a 1k sample to get your Rouge/F1.
2) Run Q4_0 variants same subset; measure delta. If delta <1.5% (your tolerance?), Q4 is a go.
3) Try INT8 on the worst-performing 100 samples to inspect systematic failure modes.

Operational notes and costs:
- Cache-warm play adds an operational script (~2–3 engineering days) to persist and restore session keys if you want deterministic high hit-rate from day-1.
- We can include 40 compute hours as pilot credits to run the three eval stages and provide a short report.
